title: Survodutide: GLP-1/Glucagon Dual Agonist — Phase 3 Research Dossier
excerpt: Survodutide (BI 456906) is Boehringer Ingelheim and Zealand Pharma's oxyntomodulin-like GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist. Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-2 results released October 2026 confirm efficacy in type 2 diabetes.

What Is Survodutide?

Survodutide (BI 456906) is an investigational once-weekly injectable dual agonist of the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, developed through a collaboration between Boehringer Ingelheim and Zealand Pharma. Structurally, it is an oxyntomodulin analog engineered from a naturally occurring gut hormone that weakly activates both receptor types, with substantially enhanced potency and prolonged half-life.

Mechanism of Action

  • GLP-1 receptor activation: Stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, slows gastric emptying, and reduces food intake via hypothalamic satiety centers.
  • Glucagon receptor activation: Increases hepatic fat oxidation, raises energy expenditure via thermogenesis, reduces ectopic lipid accumulation. Directly targets hepatic lipotoxicity implicated in MASH.

Key Research Findings

Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-1 (NEJM)

  • Mean weight loss: −16.6% with survodutide 6.0 mg vs −3.2% with placebo at 76 weeks
  • ~72% of participants lost ≥5% body weight
  • Published in the New England Journal of Medicine

Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-2 (October 2026)

  • Weight loss up to −13.1% at 76 weeks in obesity with type 2 diabetes; met both co-primary endpoints
  • Significant HbA1c and fasting glucose reductions

Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-MASLD

  • Significant reductions in liver fat (MRI-PDFF) and visceral fat beyond weight loss effects alone
  • Glucagon receptor component drives preferential hepatic fat reduction

Dosing in Research

Investigational doses: 0.6 mg to 6.0 mg weekly via subcutaneous injection. Not approved for human use outside clinical trials.

Frequently Asked Questions

How does survodutide compare to semaglutide?

Phase 3 data: −16.6% (survodutide) vs ~15% (semaglutide STEP-1). Survodutide adds glucagon-mediated hepatic fat oxidation and thermogenesis. No head-to-head trial published.

What makes survodutide unique mechanistically?

As an oxyntomodulin analog, it activates both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors — the glucagon component drives hepatic fat reduction and thermogenesis beyond what GLP-1 mono-agonists provide.

Is survodutide approved?

No. Investigational only as of October 2026. Phase 3 complete; regulatory filing expected. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

Research Limitations

  • SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT cardiovascular outcomes pending
  • LIVERAGE MASH fibrosis histological endpoints not yet published
  • No head-to-head trial against tirzepatide or semaglutide
  • Not approved anywhere as of October 2026
